newsitem.title: CANADA: No decision at Stuttgart talks on Zaire - Canada.
newsitem.headline: No decision at Stuttgart talks on Zaire - Canada.

text.p: A Stuttgart meeting on Friday of military planners on the Zaire crisis will not make any decisions on whether to send a force, Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Thursday.
"There will not be a decision in Stuttgart. It is a meeting to look at all the factors and all the options, and after that there will be a context for a decision," Axworthy said.
Asked when a decision would be made on how to proceed with the Canadian-led rescue mission, he said: "Soon...We'll make the decision when we can."

Canadian Lt. Gen. Maurice Baril, head of the U.N.-authorised mission, has been gathering information and holding discussions with central African governments. Officials had suggested he would shape the mission with other countries which have agreed to participate.

Axworthy said strategists were still trying to gather information, through reconnaissance flights and other means, to get a clearer picture of needs after the exodus to Rwanda of half a million refugees a week ago.
"I don't think anyone would want us to make a decision without the right information and having some degree of certainty," he said.
